content: Linseed oil, evening primrose oil, and bilberry capsules are a nutritional supplement approved by the FDA for dietary supplementation under the supervision of a licensed medical practitioner. The recommended dosage for adults is four softgels daily, which can be taken with or without food. It is advised to avoid taking this supplement simultaneously with other medications, medical foods, or supplements. This product is contraindicated in individuals with known hypersensitivity to any of its ingredients. Evening primrose oil, one of the components, has been associated with an increased risk of pregnancy complications and is contraindicated in pregnant women. Additionally, evening primrose oil has been linked to seizures, particularly in individuals taking phenothiazines, as it may lower the seizure threshold. Flaxseed oil, another component, may increase stool bulk and frequency. It should be used with caution in individuals with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), bowel obstruction, or diverticular disease, as it may cause ileus or thyroid issues. Both flaxseed oil and evening primrose oil may slow blood clotting, so individuals with blood disorders or those taking anticoagulant or antiplatelet medications should consult their healthcare provider before use. Blood clotting times may need to be monitored. Adverse reactions may include hypersensitivity, such as breathing difficulties, chest tightness, chest pain, skin hives, rash, itching, or swelling. Gastrointestinal upset, nausea, and headaches have also been reported. If any of these symptoms occur, the product should be discontinued, and a healthcare provider should be consulted. Flaxseed oil may interact with blood-thinning medications, increasing the risk of bleeding. Evening primrose oil may also interact with blood-thinning medications and phenothiazines, potentially increasing the risk of seizures. Bilberry, another component, has been shown to lower blood sugar levels, which may lead to dangerously low blood sugar when taken with diabetes medications. This product is contraindicated during pregnancy due to the potential for complications. There is no established safety information for use during labor, delivery, nursing, or in pediatric, geriatric, or immunocompromised populations. Additionally, there is no specific guidance for use in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment, or in relation to gender or racial populations. The product is administered orally, and there is limited information regarding its pharmacology, mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology. In case of suspected overdose, the National Poison Help hotline should be contacted immediately. The capsules are supplied as oval, dark brown soft gelatin capsules imprinted with “V232” and are dispensed in bottles containing 120 softgels. There is no specific information provided regarding storage conditions. Alcohol interaction with this product has not been established, and patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol use while taking this supplement.
